name: Zitting Cisticola
fact: A small grassland bird recorded in Sri Lanka. Breeding males call repeatedly during zigzagging display flights.
quip: A name you can mispronounce with complete scientific authority.
credit: This image has been extracted from another file
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping. Source crop by Boylarva99.

name: Great Thick-knee
fact: Also known as Great Stone-curlew, this large wader breeds in Sri Lanka. Its heavy bill handles prey along shores and riverbanks.
quip: A remarkably personal remark to publish about a bird.
credit: Own work , from Sharp Photography, sharpphotography.co.uk
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Sandwich Tern
fact: A coastal tern recorded in Sri Lanka. It catches fish by plunge-diving and may offer fish during courtship.
quip: The committee may have been approaching lunchtime.
credit: Own work , from Sharp Photography, sharpphotography.co.uk
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Greater Racket-tailed Drongo
fact: A forest bird with two long outer tail feathers ending in racket-like tips. It can imitate other birds and join mixed-species feeding flocks.
quip: A name that needs its own luggage allowance.
credit: Own work. Source copyright notice: Dr Ashok Kolluru, 2022.
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Coppersmith Barbet
fact: A small green barbet whose repeated call resembles metal being hammered. It feeds largely on fruit and excavates a nest in wood.
quip: Your uncle says he knows a good one.
credit: Own work
changes: Source signature removal and corrections by Archaeodontosaurus. Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Lesser Whistling-Duck
fact: A duck that breeds across the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. It often feeds at night and gathers around lakes and wet paddy fields by day.
quip: A duck named after a talent show and a disappointing review.
credit: Dendrocygna javanica - Chiang Mai. Own work.
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Brown Boobook
fact: An owl also known as Brown Hawk-Owl. It breeds in Sri Lanka and hunts large insects and small animals in wooded habitats.

artist: Lip Kee from Singapore, Republic of Singapore
credit: Brown Hawk Owl (Ninox scutulata scutulata)
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Watercock
fact: A wetland bird in the rail family, recorded in Sri Lanka. Its long toes help it move through marsh vegetation.
quip: The naming committee appears to have consulted a plumber.
credit: Own work
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Cotton Pygmy-Goose
fact: Despite its name, this is a tiny duck. It uses waters rich in vegetation and nests in tree holes.
quip: Three perfectly ordinary words, left unsupervised.
credit: Own work
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Lesser Adjutant
fact: A large stork with a mostly bare head and neck. It stalks small animals in lowland wetlands.

credit: Own work, from Sharp Photography, sharpphotography.co.uk.
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Dollarbird
fact: A roller with pale, coin-like patches in its wings. It launches from exposed perches to catch flying insects.
quip: A very strong choice for a bird with no income.
credit: Own work
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Sri Lanka Hanging-Parrot
fact: A small, short-tailed parrot endemic to Sri Lanka. Adults have red on the crown and rump and pale blue on the throat.

credit: Own work
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Sri Lanka Frogmouth
subject: Name the bird resting on the nest.
fact: A nocturnal forest bird found in Sri Lanka and southern India. Its leaf-like plumage camouflages it among branches during the day.
quip: Someone looked at that face and chose permanent consequences.
credit: Own work , from Sharp Photography, sharpphotography.co.uk
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Oriental Darter
fact: A waterbird with a long neck and pointed bill. It hunts fish while swimming underwater.
quip: Darter. A bird name with suspiciously pub-sport energy.
credit: Own work
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Knob-billed Duck

quip: They printed “Knob-billed Duck” in a book and sold the book to adults.
credit: Own work , from Sharp Photography, sharpphotography.co.uk
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Fork-tailed Drongo-Cuckoo
fact: This glossy black cuckoo resembles a drongo and occurs in Sri Lanka. It keeps to wooded habitats and gives a series of whistles that rise in pitch.
occurrenceEvidence: Ceylon Bird Club July 2026 list, entry 38, PDF page 3; also on Avibase Sri Lanka checklist.
quip: Three bird-naming ideas in one trench coat.

changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Whiskered Tern

occurrenceEvidence: Ceylon Bird Club July 2026 list, entry 143, PDF page 6; also on Avibase Sri Lanka checklist.
quip: A seabird named by the facial-hair subcommittee.
credit: Own work , from Sharp Photography, sharpphotography.co.uk
changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

fact: A brown tropical seabird with a pale crown. It feeds by swooping low over the water and dipping down for small fish and other prey.
occurrenceEvidence: Ceylon Bird Club July 2026 list, entry 135, PDF page 6; also on Avibase Sri Lanka checklist.

changes: Resized for the web; complete source frame shown without additional cropping.

name: Brown-capped Babbler
fact: Found only in Sri Lanka, this shy insect-eater keeps to forest undergrowth. Its loud calls often give away its hiding place.
occurrenceEvidence: Ceylon Bird Club July 2026 list, entry 387, PDF page 13; also on Avibase Sri Lanka checklist.
quip: One sensible hat and absolutely no indoor voice.
credit: Brown-capped Babbler (Pellorneum fuscocapillus)

name: Ruddy Turnstone
fact: This stocky shorebird flips stones and seaweed to uncover small animals. It breeds far to the north and winters on coasts around the world.
occurrenceEvidence: Ceylon Bird Club July 2026 list, entry 107, PDF page 5; also on Avibase Sri Lanka checklist.
quip: A bird named like someone muttering at a difficult garden chore.
